fact: A giant of the Keel and a corner of the 'False Cross' — with a name coined in the age of flight.
bio: Avior (Epsilon Carinae) is a system about 600 light-years away pairing an orange giant with a hot blue companion. It sits in Carina, forming one corner of the False Cross that is often mistaken for the true Southern Cross.
cultural: Avior is one of the few star names with no ancient roots — it was assigned in the 1930s for a British air-navigation almanac, when unnamed but bright southern stars needed labels for aviators and sailors.
